name: The Samaritan leper who returned
charge: One of ten: turning back to glorify God with a loud voice, and giving thanks at his feet
summary: Ten lepers stood far off and cried for mercy, and were sent to show themselves to the priests as the law requires, and were cleansed as they went (Luke 17:11-14). Nine kept going. One turned back, glorified God with a loud voice and fell on his face at Christ’s feet giving thanks, and Luke names him a Samaritan, that is, an Israelite of the northern kingdom (Luke 17:15-16). He alone was asked after and told that his faith had made him whole (Luke 17:17-19).
offenseFull: Passing through the midst of Samaria and Galilee, he entered a village and ten men that were lepers met him, standing far off, and lifted up their voices for mercy; he told them to go and show themselves to the priests, and as they went they were cleansed (Luke 17:11-14). The order was the law. When he cleansed a leper earlier he charged the man to tell no one, but to go and show himself to the priest and offer for his cleansing according as Moses commanded, for a testimony (Luke 5:12-14), and that offering is set out in the law of the leper (Leviticus 14:2-4). Christ did not set the statute aside; he sent men to keep it. They moved on his word before the record says a thing about them being healed.

One of them, seeing that he was healed, turned back and glorified God with a loud voice, and fell down on his face at his feet giving thanks; and Luke adds that he was a Samaritan (Luke 17:15-16). That does not mean another nation. Samaria held Israelites: the woman at the well asked whether he was greater than their father Jacob, and the record notes that the Jews had no dealings with the Samaritans (John 4:9; John 4:12). The man Christ goes on to call a stranger is an Israelite of the northern kingdom, and the scriptures use the word that way. The sons of the stranger who join themselves to the Lord, keep the sabbath and take hold of his covenant are brought to the holy mountain and their sacrifices accepted (Isaiah 56:6-7), and the strangers gathered with Judah and Benjamin came out of Ephraim and Manasseh and Simeon, and entered into a covenant to seek the Lord with all their heart (2 Chronicles 15:9; 2 Chronicles 15:12).
judgmentFull: He asked whether there were not ten cleansed, where the other nine were, and why none was found returning to give glory to God except this stranger, and then told the man to arise and go his way, for his faith had made him whole (Luke 17:17-19). All ten were cleansed; one was commended. The thing named is faith, and faith is what marks the children of Abraham, for they which are of faith are the children of Abraham (Galatians 3:7). Israel did not obtain that which it sought, but the election obtained it and the rest were blinded (Romans 11:7). The nine were of the blood. The one who came back had the faith with it.

The account does not announce the end of the nine or take back what was given them. It makes their absence a question that has to be answered. Thanksgiving belongs together with the mercy received: the man who offers praise glorifies God (Psalms 50:23), and the charge is to bless the Lord and forget none of his benefits, who forgives all iniquities and heals all diseases (Psalms 103:1-3). This man did not forget once the trouble was lifted off him. He turned around and went back to the one who lifted it.

text.text: And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
And as he entered into a certain village, there met him ten men that were lepers, which stood afar off:
And they lifted up their voices, and said, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.
And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed.
And it came to pass, when he was in a certain city, behold a man full of leprosy: who seeing Jesus fell on his face, and besought him, saying, Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
And he put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will: be thou clean. And immediately the leprosy departed from him.
And he charged him to tell no man: but go, and shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing, according as Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
This shall be the law of the leper in the day of his cleansing: He shall be brought unto the priest:
And the priest shall go forth out of the camp; and the priest shall look, and, behold, if the plague of leprosy be healed in the leper;
Then shall the priest command to take for him that is to be cleansed two birds alive and clean, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop:
And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God,
And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan.
Then saith the woman of Samaria unto him, How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.
Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well, and drank thereof himself, and his children, and his cattle?

Also the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to the Lord, to serve him, and to love the name of the Lord, to be his servants, every one that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and taketh hold of my covenant;

Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.

And he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Israel in abundance, when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.
And they entered into a covenant to seek the Lord God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul;
And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?
There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger.
And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.
Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.
What then? Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for; but the election hath obtained it, and the rest were blinded
Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God.
Bless the Lord, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name.
Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:
Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases;
